awa001.description: In this video, Shailendra Kumar Mishra, a farmer and a speaker of the Allahabadi variety of the Awadhi language from Allahabad, Uttar Pradesh, India, discusses the agricultural practices in his village. Interviewed by Subhashish Panigrahi for the OpenSpeaks Archives, with support from Abhinav Srivastava of Azad Reads and Harshavardhan Mishra. In the interview, Shailendra briefly shares which crops he and his family grow year-round and how they make paneer from milk.
awa001.title: Illahabadi-Awadhi documentation: Discussion on agriculture
bfw001.description: Gobardhan Panda, a researcher of Bonda language, recites the Bonda origin myth in the form of a poem he wrote in the Bonda language. He also translates the meaning of the stanzas in the Odia language. Recorded by Prateek Pattanaik in 2018 for the production of Remosam, a 2019 documentary by Subhashish Panigrahi. This footage was unused in the film and edited and published under the Munaremo project in 2024. Subtitled by Gobardhan Panda and Subhashish Panigrahi.
bfw001.title: Story
bfw002.description: In this monologue, Gobardhan Panda, an autodidact anthropologist from Koraput, Odisha, India, shows body parts and says their names in the Bonda language. Recorded by Prateek Pattanaik in 2018 for the production of Remosam, a 2019 documentary by Subhashish Panigrahi. The footage was unused in the film and was edited and published under the Munaremo project in 2024. Subtitling by Subhashish Panigrahi using the 1998 book Remosam as a reference.
bfw002.title: Body parts
bfw003.description: Mangala Sisa, speaker of the Bonda language, and Gobardhan Panda, anthropologist and researcher, discuss the preparation of "Pendom", a drink similar to handia, how it was consumed during the then recently concluded Pus Porob, and drink together. Their conversations are in Bonda language with occasional use of the Desia language (marked within 'single quote' in subtitles). Recorded by Prateek Pattanaik in 2018 for the production of Remosam, a 2019 documentary by Subhashish Panigrahi. A small part of the footage was used in the film, and the longer version was edited and published in the Munaremo project in 2024. Subtitling by Gobardhan Panda and Subhashish Panigrahi using Panda's 1998 book Remosam as a reference.
bfw003.title: Pendom
bfw004.description: In this video interview, Sukra Dhangdamajhi, a disari (Bonda shaman) from Malkangiri district, Odisha, India, shares his shamanic practices. Gobardhan Panda, a researcher of the Bonda language and the interviewer, and Dhangdamajhi speak in the Bonda language with occasional use of Desia, a lingua franca among Bonda, Gutob, Odia and other local communities. Desia parts are indicated within quotes (e.g. 'ନି-ନା, ସେରମୂଲ୍') in the Odia TimedText subtitles. Recorded by Prateek Pattanaik in 2018 for the production of Remosam, a 2019 documentary by Subhashish Panigrahi. This footage was partially used in the film and was later edited and published under the Munaremo project in 2024 by Panigrahi. Subtitled from Bonda to Odia by Gobardhan Panda and from Odia to English by Panigrahi, who also edited the Odia subtitles for clarity.
bfw004.title: Shamanism
gbm001.description: In this video, Sampati, a speaker of Jaunpuri, a dialect of the Garhwali language of India and a resident of Dewalsari from the Garhwal region of the Uttarakhand state, discusses the use of Aadhaar and public information access-related issues on 8 November 2019. Interviewed by Subhashish Panigrahi for the latter's 2021 documentary film, MarginalizedAadhaar. Unused or trimmed archival footage from the film was edited by Panigrahi and published as part of the OpenSpeaks Archives project in 2026. Hindi subtitles are by Arun Gour and Manoj Bilwal.
gbm001.title: Information Access and Aadhaar
gbm002.description: In this video, Surendra Dutt, a Jaunpuri speaker from Bangseel, Uttarakhand, India, discusses the state of his farming occupation at the time of recording in 2019. Interview conducted and recorded by Subhashish Panigrahi on location for his 2021 documentary film, MarginalizedAadhaar.

gju001.description: Self introduction of Taukeer Alam in Van Gujjari, a variety of the Gujari language. Recorded by Subhashish Panigrahi 2019 for the production of his 2021 documentary, MarginalizedAadhaar. The footage was unused in the film and was edited and published under the मारी जबान मारी बिरसा (Maari Jaban Maari Birsa) project in 2024. Van Gujjari and Hindi subtitles by Alam, translation to English by Panigrahi. Video and subtitles edited by Panigrahi.

gju003.description: In this interview, Taukeer Alam talks briefly about different Van Gujjar cultural festivals, detailing on unique wedding rituals and clothing in his native language, Van Gujjari. hoc002.description: In this interview, Mangal Singhku, a speaker of the Ho language, narrates the rituals of Guan Bunga, a religious ceremony of the Ho community of India. Guan Bunga, literally, "cattle pen worship", is performed by the family head, "desauli". Recorded by Subhashish Panigrahi at Keshpada, Mayurbhanj district, Odisha, India, for his 2019 documentary Mage Porob. Multiple videos unused/less used in the film were edited by Panigrahi into a single short documentary and published under the 𑢼𑣃𑣃𑣊 𑢾𑣁𑣌𑣁𑣖 (Ruum Sakam) project in 2024. hoc003.description: In this interview, Ramai Singh and his friend briefly play a tune of the Mage Porob, a traditional festival of the Ho people. Singh is seen playing dama while his friend plays dumang and they explain to Lalit Singh Banra how these folk percussion instruments are made. Singh, his friend and Banra speak in the Ho language. Recorded by Subhashish Panigrahi at Keshpada, Mayurbhanj district, Odisha, India, for his 2019 documentary Mage Porob. The footage was unused in the film and was edited and published under the 𑢼𑣃𑣃𑣊 𑢾𑣁𑣌𑣁𑣖 (Ruum Sakam) project in 2024. Ho subtitles and translation to Odia and English by Ganesh Birua, and subtitles edited by Panigrahi.
hoc003.title: Dama and Dumang
hoc004.description: In this interview, Sunaram Singh Tiyu, a farmer from Keshpada, Mayurbhanj district, Odisha, India, shares with Lalit Singh Banra about his occupation. kfy001.description: This video is taken from Johari (original title: जोहारी), the eponymous 2026 short film by Subhashish Panigrahi. The film, part of the OpenSpeaks Archives, uses archival footage from the production of Panigrahi's 2021 documentary Marginalized Aadhaar. Johari features interviews with Surendra Singh Pangtey, a native speaker of the Johari dialect of the Kumaoni language, author, and former Indian Army and Indian Administrative Service officer. He speaks in two major forms of Johari. One form is used in highly context-specific environments, mostly historically, such as when two Shauka individuals on horses meet for a very brief moment as their horses cross paths. This form uses a wide set of words from the now-extinct Rankas and Shaukiya-Khun, both forms used by the tribe in the past. The other, second form is used in everyday conversation by the Shauka people, known as Johari.
kfy001.title: Introduction
kfy002.description: Surendra Singh Pangtey narrates the origin story with a historic account in Johari
kfy002.title: Myth & History
kfy003.description: This video is taken from Johari (original title: जोहारी), a 2026 short film by Subhashish Panigrahi. The film, part of the OpenSpeaks Archives, uses archival footage from the production of Panigrahi's 2021 documentary Marginalized Aadhaar. Johari features interviews with Surendra Singh Pangtey, a native Johari speaker, author, and former Indian Army and Indian Administrative Service officer. He speaks in two major forms. One form is used in highly context-specific environments, such as when two Shauka individuals on horses meet for a very brief moment as their horses cross paths. This form uses a wide set of words from the now-extinct Rankas and Shaukiya-Khun, both forms used by the tribe in the past. The other, second form is used in everyday conversation by the Shauka people, known as Johari. Chapters a. Torn Shoes (Joke) In this tiny snippet, Pangtey narrates a joke where a pun is used to narrate how a small pronunciation twist can alter a situation. He speaks in a particular form of Johari, using words from Shaukiya-Khun, a tongue now extinct.
kfy003.title: Torn Shoes (Joke)

kgg001.description: In this conversation with Uday Raj Aaley, the late Gyani Maiya Sen-Kusunda (1937–2020), a community elder from Dang, Nepal, says the names of body parts in her native language, Kusunda. This video is from footage unused in the film and was edited and published under the Gejmehac Gipan project in 2024. Nepali subtitles are by Aaley, and English translations are by Panigrahi.

kgg002.description: In this brief conversation with Uday Raj Aaley, the late Gyani Maiya Sen-Kusunda (1937–2020), a Kusunda community elder from Dang, Nepal, shares how the Kusunda people used to cook during their semi-nomadic days in forests, in her native language, Kusunda. Recorded by Subhashish Panigrahi in 2018 for the production of his 2019 documentary film, Gyani Maiya. Unused or trimmed, archival footage from the film was edited by Panigrahi and published under the Gejmehac Gipan project in 2025. Kusunda and Nepali subtitles are by Aaley, and English translations by Panigrahi.

kgg003.description: In this conversation with Uday Raj Aaley, the late Gyani Maiya Sen-Kusunda (1937–2020), a Kusunda community elder from Dang, Nepal, discusses the endangerment of her native language, Kusunda. Recorded by Subhashish Panigrahi in 2018 for the production of his 2019 documentary film, Gyani Maiya. Unused or trimmed, archival footage from the film was edited by Panigrahi and published under the Gejmehac Gipan project in 2025. Kusunda and Nepali subtitles are by Aaley, and English translations are by Sanjib Chaudhary and Panigrahi.
kgg003.title: Kusunda language endangerment
kgg004.description: In this conversation with Uday Raj Aaley, the late Gyani Maiya Sen-Kusunda (1937–2020), a community elder from Kulmor, Dang district, Nepal, shares the nomadic part of her life in the forest in her native language, Kusunda (known to the community as "Gejmehac Gipan", literally, the "forest king's language"). Her community left the nomadic life and settled in villages around the district. Recorded by Subhashish Panigrahi in 2018 for the production of his 2019 documentary film, Gyani Maiya. This video was taken from the unused/less used film footage, edited, and published under the Gejmehac Gipan project in 2024. Kusunda and Nepali subtitles are by Aaley, and English translations are by Panigrahi.

The original recording from 2018 includes an interview in which Gyani Maiya Sen-Kusunda answers several questions asked by Uday Raj Aaley in Nepali based on broader questions by Panigrahi. Sen-Kusunda answers mostly in Kusunda and occasionally in Nepali.

kip001.description: In this video, Tika Kumari Budha, a childhood development trainer from Jungkot, Rolpa district, Nepal, speaks in the Sheshi Kham variety of the Kham Magar language. Interviewed by Uday Raj Aaley and recorded by Deewash Thapa in Jungkot on 17 July 2026 for OpenSpeaks Archives. She talks about her family's farming year, with corn sown in the Jeth (Jyeshtha) and Baisakh months, barley and wheat in November and December, and mustard and millet. Women wove aloe fibre into thread and mats while men sowed and ploughed, and in winter many men went to Butwal, Bhairawa, Kathmandu and India or other countries abroad to earn money. Sheshi Kham and Nepali subtitles are by Budha, transcribed and typed by Aaley, and English translations are by Panigrahi. Video edited by Panigrahi.
kip001.title: Sheshi Kham language documentation
lmn001.description: In this video, Nenavath Mohan and Meghavath Sathish, both speakers of the Lambadi language from Telangana, India, discuss some of their community festivals: Teej, Seethla & Gharegharer. Interview conducted and recorded by Subhashish Panigrahi in Hyderabad, Telangana, on 4 September 2019 as part of his 2021 documentary film, MarginalizedAadhaar.
lmn001.title: Teej, Seethla & Gharegharer Festivals
lmn002.description: In this video, Meghavath Sathish and Nenavath Mohan, both from Telangana, India, and speakers of the Lambadi language, discuss Aadhaar, the Indian digital ID, in the context of their community life. They were interviewed on the 4th September, 2019, in Hyderabad, Telangana, by Subhashish Panigrahi, a Baleswari-Odia-language speaker, for the documentary film MarginalizedAadhaar. The interview was subtitled in Hindi at the location by Panigrahi, based on a verbatim translation by Meghavath and Nenavath. Footage, some of which was used in the film, and subtitles were edited and translated into English by Panigrahi, and were published under the OpenSpeaks Archives project in 2026.
lmn002.title: Problems for not Having Aadhaar

lmn004.description: In this audio, Nenavath Mohan, a native speaker of Lambadi language, pronounces "Lambada" (Lambadi). It is derived from a longer conversation between Nenavath and Meghavath Sathish, also a native Lambadi speaker. They both discusses Aadhaar, the Indian digital ID, in the context of their community life in a village in Vikarabad district, Telangana, India. They were interviewed on the 4th September, 2019, in Hyderabad, Telangana, by Subhashish Panigrahi, a Baleswari-Odia-language speaker, for the documentary film MarginalizedAadhaar. The interview was partially subtitled in Hindi at the location by Panigrahi, based on a verbatim translation by Meghavath and Nenavath. Footage, some of which was used in the film, and subtitles, all later translated and reviewed by Nenavath, were edited and translated into English by Panigrahi and were published under the OpenSpeaks Archives project in 2026.

sci001.description: In this video, Sajehan Buckman, a speaker of the Sri Lankan Malay language from Colombo, Sri Lanka, discusses the origin of his community and their migration from present-day Indonesia and Malaysia to Sri Lanka. Buckman was interviewed on 19 February, 2026 by Subhashish Panigrahi and Omar Rajaraman in Colombo.

srb001.description: In this video, Ramani Dalbehera, a speaker of the Sora language of India and a resident of Rayagada district from the Odisha state, discusses her experience with Aadhaar, India's biometric ID. Dalbehera was interviewed in 2019 by Opino Gomango and Subhashish Panigrahi for the latter's 2021 documentary film, MarginalizedAadhaar. The interview took place in Sora with Gomango, in the presence of Namad Dalbehera, another Lanjia-Sora speaker who is related to Ramani. Gomango asked more detailed and nuanced questions based on the broader questions/structure set by Panigrahi in Odia. Unused or trimmed archival footage from the film was edited by Panigrahi and published under the OpenSpeaks Archives project in 2026. English subtitles by Gomango, and edits and Odia subtitles are by Panigrahi.

thq001.description: In this video, Achhai Chaudhary, a speaker of the Eastern (Saptariya) Tharu language of Nepal and a resident of Saptari District from the Madhesh Province of Nepal, shares about the medicinal properties of several local plants in his native language, Eastern (Saptariya) Tharu, in 2025. Interviewed by Sanjib Chaudhary. Unused or trimmed archival footage from the film was edited by Subhashish Panigrahi and published under the OpenSpeaks Archives project in 2026. Eastern Tharu, Nepali, and English subtitles are by Sanjib Chaudhary, and the subtitles are edited by Panigrahi.
